caption: The drawing is a black and white illustration depicting a metallic pitcher with a handle and a spout, labeled "Pitcher for Measuring" at the top. The pitcher has a slightly flared rim forming a spout on the left side, and a distinct handle on the right that curves outward before looping back towards the body of the vessel. The surface of the pitcher is shaded to indicate a metallic texture, and there are volume markings visible inside the upper rim, with “500” written on the inner wall. The pitcher sits on a circular base and casts a shadow to the lower right. The numbers "No 51" and "Case 4" are written in the lower left corner. In the lower right corner, the name "Alfred Nason" and the date "Jan 15th 1936" are written in cursive and block letters. The illustration is rendered on a plain, light background with a simple rectangular border.
title: Pewter Pitcher
